bugs: Empty query params (`?status=`, `?from=`, `?country=`) return 422 instead of using the defaults, because the rules are 'sometimes' without 'nullable' and ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns '' into null (app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:21-24). Defensible strictness, but `?status=` failing next to a 'default paid' rule is unfriendly.
`?to=2026-03-01&from=garbage` returns an extra, misleading after_or_equal error on 'to' as well as the real 'from' error (SalesReportRequest.php:22).
antipatterns: tests/Feature/SalesReportTest.php:250 test_the_endpoint_makes_no_network_calls: Http::fake plus assertNothingSent tests nothing meaningful for this feature

app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:31-38 filters() returns raw date strings and app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:46-47 parses them into Carbon later, so the request DTO is only half-typed (status is an enum, dates are strings)
app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:32 echoes the filters back with a spread-then-override trick, which goes beyond the spec
SalesReportRequest.php:13-15 prepareForValidation strtoupper is fine, but it relies on TrimStrings implicitly
strengths: Money shape is the same everywhere ({cents, formatted}) through a single money() helper using Number::currency
Uses Laravel 13 #[Scope] and #[Fillable] attributes, enum cast, Rule::enum, and a typed array-shape docblock on filters()
One reusable $matching closure is applied through tap() and whereHas, so every section shares the same filters
Strict Y-m-d date_format, plus endOfDay inclusive ranges with qualified column names in the scopes
Aggregation stays in SQL with deterministic tie-breakers (sku, email) and toBase() to avoid hydrating models

Thorough tests: exact JSON for the empty report, inclusive boundaries, unit_price versus current product price, rounding, thousand separators, and a data provider of invalid inputs including array injection and an impossible date
Migrations have sensible FK actions (cascade on order, restrict on product) and indexes

bugs: Money is shaped inconsistently in the API: total_revenue and average_order_value are {cents, formatted} objects, but revenue_per_country, top_products and top_customers use flat revenue_cents/revenue_formatted and spend_cents/spend_formatted keys (app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:58,77,97,117-120). Consumers have to handle two money contracts.
The 'date' rule is lenient: it accepts ISO datetimes such as 2026-03-01T00:00:00 and other strtotime-parsable formats, then silently truncates them to the day (SalesReportRequest.php:22-23)
antipatterns: app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:109-125 three money helpers (money, moneyFields, format) exist only to support the inconsistent output shape
app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:101-104 lineTotal() is a method returning a constant string where a class constant would do
app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:15 trim() duplicates the global TrimStrings middleware
app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:40 OrderStatus::tryFrom($data['status'] ?? '') ?? Paid is roundabout compared with validated('status', default)
database/migrations/2026_11_07_205617_create_order_items_table.php:19 redundant index('product_id') on a constrained foreignId
app/Models/Product.php:17-20 and OrderItem.php:19-22 add integer casts that are noise
tests/Feature/SalesReportTest.php:22 app(Http::class)->preventStrayRequests() instead of the Http facade, with an aliased client factory import
tests/Feature/SalesReportTest.php:27 stringly-typed dynamic factory state call ->{$state}()
strengths: The request converts input into typed CarbonImmutable values (startOfDay/endOfDay) and an enum, then spreads them into named report arguments
sometimes|nullable means empty params fall back to the defaults, and a test covers this
An OrderItem forOrders scope uses a whereIn subquery, and closure factories rebuild fresh builders for each section
Good tests: country filter checked across every section, ranking with cumulative product revenue, behaviour without an Accept header, and a data provider for 422 cases

v.rationale: Both implementations have nearly the same architecture: an invokable controller, a FormRequest, a BuildSalesReport invokable class, Laravel 13 #[Scope]/#[Fillable] attributes and SQL aggregation. impl-2 ranks first because its API contract is cleaner and consistent: every money value is a {cents, formatted} object from one helper, and date validation is strict Y-m-d. impl-1 returns two money shapes: nested objects at the top level, and flat *_cents/*_formatted keys in the per-country, product and customer lists. That is a real contract defect, and it needed extra helpers (money, moneyFields, format, plus lineTotal) to produce. impl-1 also has small redundancies: a trim that TrimStrings already does, a redundant index, and unneeded integer casts. impl-1 does handle empty query params more gracefully. impl-2 returns 422 for `?status=` and `?from=`, and adds a noisy extra error on 'to' when 'from' is invalid. Those are smaller issues than an inconsistent response shape. impl-2's tests are a bit more precise (exact JSON for the empty report, an impossible-date case, thousand separators), though it includes one pointless network-call test.
